DUMMY/3993.wav|porta-um performance while for porta billing or porta sip, the majority of resources are used during call initiation or call disconnect, with porta-um the situation is different. porta-um is a media server providing ivr services, which means that all the voice traffic must go through it. when a call is in progress, hundreds of rtp packets must be processed each second with minimal delay. in order to maintain an acceptable sound quality. this limits the number of concurrent calls which a single portaum server can process. of course, you can scale up with multiple portaum servers to achieve the required performance. on a standard server, portaum can handle about one thousand five hundred incoming ivr sessions. for applications such as auto attendant or balance info, or about seven hundred and fifty concurrent two-way ivr sessions, for example, for prepaid card or callback applications, when there is an incoming call from the user to portaum and an outgoing call from portaum to another destination. another limitation on portaum is the number of mailboxes the server can store. each mailbox, even an empty one, takes up a certain amount of disk space for storing message data. therefore, a assuming a maximum allowed mailbox size of ten MB, around one GB of disk space will be enough to store about one thousand user mailboxes. perhaps you are planning on processing more ivr calls than a single server can handle. in this case, you can install several portaum servers, combined into a single cluster. incoming calls are dynamically distributed across all servers in the cluster to provide optimal performance. besides an increased total capacity, this greatly increases the fault tolerance of the whole system since the failure of a single server does not affect service. portaum is capable of maintaining up to one hundred thousand user mailboxes and processing up to one thousand five hundred concurrent ivr sessions on a single server. multiple portaum servers may also also be combined into a cluster to improve overall system performance and increase reliability.

DUMMY/2209.wav|portasip performance a single portasip server can process up to fifty thousand concurrent registrations and fifty call attempts per second. what exactly does this mean? it means that fifty thousand IP phones can be online on your network at the same time and that up to fifty users can start a new phone call every second. how many simultaneous or concurrent calls does that translate into? it mainly depends on the average call duration and call success rate. assuming the industry norms of an average call duration of five minutes and a call success rate of fifty percent, this adds up to seven thousand five hundred concurrent calls. this means that seven thousand five hundred of your customers can be talking on the phone at the same time. this scenario assumes that portasip is only handling signaling communications and that the media stream goes directly between endpoints. if portasip were to handle the media proxying as well. this would require the processing of a significant amount of network traffic. therefore, each server should be handling about two thousand concurrent calls to ensure that voice quality will not degrade due to packet delays. if you plan to have more subscribers or more simultaneous phone calls than this, you can scale up your network performance by adding another portasip server. this will increase not only your total network capacity but also your service reliability since the portasip servers will be working as a cluster. portasip is capable of processing fifty call initiations per second which translates into approximately seven thousand five hundred concurrent calls. for increased performance you can use multiple portasip servers combined into a cluster.

DUMMY/2139.wav|porta um performance while for porta billing one hundred or portasip, the majority of resources are used during call initiation or call disconnect, with porta um the situation is different. porta um is a media server providing ivr services, which means that all the voice traffic must go through it. when a call is in progress, hundreds of rtp packets must be processed each second with minimal delay. in order to maintain an acceptable sound quality. this limits the number of concurrent calls which a single portaum server can process. of course, you can scale up with multiple portaum servers to achieve the required performance. on a standard server, portaum can handle about five hundred incoming ivr sessions for applications such as auto-attendant or balance info, or about two hundred and fifty concurrent two-way ivr sessions. for example, for prepaid card or callback applications, when there is an incoming call from the user to portaum and an outgoing call from portaum to another destination. another limitation on portaum is the number of mailboxes the server can store. each mailbox, even an empty one, takes up a certain amount of disk space for storing message data. therefore, assuming a maximum allowed mailbox size of ten MB, around one GB of disk space will be enough to store about a thousand user mailboxes.

milliliter. the lumjev u two hundred pre-filled pen contains two times as much insulin per one milliliter as standard u one hundred insulin. the dose window on the pens shows the number of units of including if you have heart failure or other heart, liver, or kidney problems, if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or plan to become pregnant or breastfeed. how to take. read the instructions for use insulin you take. before injecting your lumgev, you can inject your insulin dose yourself, or you can have a trained caregiver inject it for you. make sure you or your caregiver check the insulin label before each injection. this will help you make sure you're taking the correct insulin. use a new needle for each injection. you can get a serious infection or the wrong dose of insulin if you reuse needles. change, rotate where you inject your insulin with each dose. this can reduce your chance of getting pits, lumps, or thickened skin where you inject your insulin. do not inject your
